question: What is the main purpose of surgery when treating an early-stage solid tumor?

options.A: To destroy rapidly dividing systemic cells
options.C: To remove the primary tumor mass
options.D: To stimulate the patient immune system

explanation: Surgery involves physically cutting out the localized tumor tissue to control or cure the cancer. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is chemotherapy considered a systemic treatment?

options.A: It circulates through the entire bloodstream to reach cancer cells
options.B: It only affects cells located directly inside the targeted organ
options.C: It stimulates local antibodies without entering the vascular system
options.D: It relies entirely on high-energy radiation beams from outside

explanation: Chemotherapy drugs travel through the bloodstream, allowing them to reach cancer cells anywhere in the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which major complication should a nurse watch out for after a major cancer surgery?
explanation: Having cancer and undergoing major surgery both raise the risk of blood clots forming in the deep veins. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the best way to prevent lung complications after major abdominal surgery?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake to prevent baseline edema
options.C: Apply specialized ionizing radiation shielding dressings
options.D: Encourage deep breathing and early ambulation

explanation: Deep breathing opens up the air sacs in the lungs while moving around gets the blood flowing, which stops the lungs from collapsing and prevents blood clots. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h2)

question: What must a nurse always check before giving chemotherapy through a peripheral line?
explanation: Seeing blood return confirms that the needle is securely inside the vein, preventing the drug from leaking into the surrounding tissue. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why must nurses wear protective gear when handling chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: To stop airborne bacterial transmission from the patient
options.B: To protect the nurse from catching the patient malignancy
options.C: To prevent occupational exposure to hazardous cytotoxic agents
options.D: To keep the sterile intravenous tubing completely free of dust

explanation: Chemotherapy medications are strong drugs that can touch the skin or be breathed in, so staff need barriers to stay safe. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h3)

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to care for skin undergoing radiation therapy?

options.A: Scrub the skin firmly with a rough sponge during baths
options.B: Apply strongly scented perfumed lotions twice a day
options.C: Expose the treatment field directly to strong sunlight daily
options.D: Wash the treatment area gently with mild soap and water

explanation: Gentle washing helps protect sensitive skin that has been weakened by radiation treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why does radiation therapy often cause skin breakdown?

options.A: Chemotherapy pills accumulate specifically in the subcutaneous fat layers
options.B: Ionizing radiation damages rapidly dividing basal cells in the epidermis
options.C: Surgical incisions fail to heal due to poor systemic hydration
options.D: Infection spreads rapidly from intravenous lines to the skin surface

explanation: Radiation affects normal, fast-growing skin cells along with the cancer cells, making it hard for the skin to heal and renew itself. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is a low count of white blood cells caused by cancer treatment called?
explanation: Neutropenia is the medical term for a low number of neutrophils, which are white blood cells that fight off infections. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the best way to help a patient with painful mouth sores from chemotherapy?

options.A: Encourage the patient to consume very hot, spicy local meals
options.B: Provide frequent mouth rinses with a gentle, non-alcoholic solution
options.C: Scrub the oral lesions firmly with a stiff nylon toothbrush
options.D: Restrict all fluid intake to keep the oral cavity completely dry

explanation: Gentle rinses clean the mouth and soothe sores without causing more irritation to delicate tissues. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h5)

question: What should you do first if a patient with neutropenia develops a fever?

options.A: Send the patient home to rest in a quiet environment
options.B: Wait for laboratory blood culture results for three days
options.D: Apply cold ice packs to reduce systemic body temperature

explanation: Fever in a neutropenic patient is a medical emergency that needs immediate antibiotics to prevent severe infection. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h6)

question: What causes tumor lysis syndrome to happen?

options.A: Rapid destruction of cancer cells releasing intracellular ions into blood
options.B: Sudden uncontrolled bleeding caused by severe bone marrow platelet failure
options.C: Infection spreading from the gastrointestinal tract into the bloodstream
options.D: Severe compression of the superior vena cava by a growing chest tumor

explanation: When cancer cells break down rapidly, they release cell contents into the blood faster than the kidneys can filter them out. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is cancer-related weight loss (cachexia) hard to fix just by eating more food?

options.A: Chemotherapy drugs destroy the stomach lining permanently forever
options.B: Vitamins and minerals cannot be absorbed through human intestines
options.C: It involves complex metabolic and inflammatory alterations in the body
options.D: Patients simply refuse to eat because they dislike hospital food

explanation: Cachexia changes how the body handles proteins and energy due to inflammation, rather than just happening because the person is eating less. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h7)

question: Which meal plan works best for a cancer patient who gets full quickly and has a poor appetite?

options.A: Serving small, frequent, nutrient-dense meals throughout the day
options.B: Restricting fluid intake completely during all daily waking hours
options.C: Forcing three large heavy meals regardless of patient comfort
options.D: Providing only clear water and plain broth for all nutrition

explanation: Eating small amounts often prevents the patient from feeling too full and helps them take in enough calories. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h7)

question: When is the best time to introduce palliative care for a patient with a serious cancer diagnosis?

options.A: After all medical and surgical treatment options fail completely
options.B: Only during the final twenty-four hours of active dying
options.C: Early in the disease trajectory alongside curative treatment
options.D: When the patient requests discontinuation of all nursing care

explanation: Palliative care improves comfort and quality of life, and it works best when started early while the patient is still receiving active treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h8)

question: What is the main goal of adding palliative care to cancer treatment?

options.A: Accelerating the terminal disease process to reduce hospital costs
options.B: Preventing family members from visiting the patient in the ward
options.C: Improving quality of life by managing pain and emotional distress
options.D: Replacing all standard chemotherapy protocols with herbal medicine

explanation: Palliative care focuses on whole-person comfort, helping manage physical symptoms and emotional stress for both the patient and their family. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h8)
